articles.standfirst: El tribunal de quiebras permite a LIV Golf su reestructuración, pero desde la superliga denuncia que el DP World Tour ha querido interferir en su proceso
articles.summary: El tribunal de quiebras permite a LIV Golf su reestructuración, pero desde la superliga denuncia que el DP World Tour ha querido interferir en su proceso
articles.body: Sobre el papel, hoy es un gran día para LIV Golf. El juez encargado de su caso de quiebra ha aprobado la reestructuración empresarial junto a BC Partners -el inversor-, superando así un obstáculo significativo, pues ahora podrán gestionar el paquete de financiación propuesto de 300 millones de dólares y crear una nueva estructura. Eso sí, los abogados de LIV han declarado en el tribunal de quiebras que “anticipan que la decisión se tomará para finales de mes” en lo que se refiere a la disolución o continuación con LIV 2.0. Dicho representantes legales también han expresado su malestar con las medidas que va tomar el DP World Tour para de alguna forma torpedearlos. En cualquier caso, si LIV Golf esperaba alfombra roja para su nueva etapa es que parecen haber olvidado su pasado. Un circuito creado a base de talonario, gracias a que arrebató talento a sus competidores, es difícil que vaya a recibir alguna ayuda por parte de estos ahora. Sin la financiación del Fondo de Inversión de Arabia Saudí (PIF), la superliga parte de una posición muy débil. En este sentido, el DP World Tour, aunque no cuente con músculo financiero, tiene un arma muy poderosa que puede sentenciar al LIV. Lo dejó claro su director ejecutivo, Guy Kinnings, el lunes en BBC Sports: "Los jugadores necesitan tomar una decisión. Como hemos dicho durante muchos años, tenemos reglas y regulaciones que están ahí para proteger nuestro Tour y que todos nuestros miembros deben respetar. Los jugadores que no estén dispuestos a cumplir con nuestras reglas y regulaciones no deberían buscar unirse a nuestro Tour". Es decir, el DPWT no dejará que ninguno de sus miembros pueda alternar con torneos del LIV y se terminó el acuerdo por un año al que había llegado con algunos golfistas. Esto nos lleva a la queja hoy de los abogados de LIV que, aunque han conseguido una victoria en los tribunales, parece que no las tienen todas consigo tras la maniobra del DP World Tour. Esto han declarado: “Seguimos monitoreando esta situación muy de cerca, y francamente, nos preocupa bastante […] Francamente, el momento en particular nos parece un claro intento de interferir en nuestro proceso, con nuestros jugadores y potencialmente con nuestra reorganización […] La libertad del jugador es la razón por la que se creó LIV Golf, y es la base de LIV Golf 2.0. […] Es lamentable que otro circuito tome una visión opuesta y presione a nuestros jugadores con una falsa elección”.

articles.title: LIV golf: Organisation concerned by DP Tour's 'attempt to interfere' in player discussions
articles.summary: LIV Golf accuses the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring process, after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on the breakaway LIV circuit next season.
articles.body:
LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring process, after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on the breakaway circuit next season.

During a court hearing on Wednesday, the attorney representing LIV said that the organisation was "quite concerned" by the stance taken by the rival DP World Tour.

Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn, the attorney representing LIV, also said that the organisation would know by the end of the month if it could continue in a 'LIV 2.0' guise.

"We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly," said Fitzgerald of the DP World Tour's position.

"The timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process with our players and potentially our reorganisation writ large.

"It also raises a lot of the same anti-competitive concerns that LIV has expressed previously regarding the way competing leagues have sought to box out and punish market participants, namely these players, from participating in LIV and really only LIV."

DP World Tour declined to comment on Fitzgerald's statement, but Guy Kinnings, its CEO, told BBC Sport on Monday that "players need to make a choice," toughening the organisation's policy on playing across the tours.

In previous years, conditional releases were struck with some top players - including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton - enabling them to play on both the DP World Tour and LIV.

"Player freedom is the reason LIV Golf was created, and it's the foundation of LIV Golf 2.0, a league built around its players," Fitzgerald added as he continued his argument in court.

"LIV has been vocal in its belief in free agency and that the best players should have greater flexibility to compete across the ecosystem. It's unfortunate that another tour is taking an opposite view and pressuring our players with false choice."

Judge Michael B. Kaplan, overseeing proceedings in the New Jersey Bankruptcy Court, replied: "The comments I have read do raise concerns."

Responding to Kaplan's request for clarity on the timeline of LIV 2.0's creation, Fitzgerald said the "two critical pieces" were structural, relating to the investment from BC Partners , and having "sufficient number of players to have a bona fide golf league signed up by 25th of this month".

"We are working hard around the clock both on the player front and on the structural front," added Fitzgerald.

Asked when he would be able to advise the court "one way or the other" whether LIV was "toggling to a wind-down" or going forward, Fitzgerald said: "We would anticipate that decision will be made by the end of the month.

"Once we have full clarity on LIV 2.0, the debtors will need to very shortly begin making payments to host sites, vendors and other parties, so that we can schedule and prepare for LIV 2.0 events that we anticipate will take place shortly following the emergence."

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding.

As part of the court-supervised "restructuring process", which the organisation hopes to conclude in early 2027, player contracts have been "rejected" and no players are obligated to be part of LIV going forward.

During Wednesday's hearing, 19 player contracts - including those of Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson - were rejected, after having been adjourned from a hearing last week because those players wanted clarity that contract rejection would enable them to have conversations with third parties about their futures.

LIV recruited a number of high profile players following its launch in 2021, but now owes its participants at least $45m (£33m).

Current Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed, who left LIV in January, has said he was accepted "from day one" after rejoining the European tour.

"This year fully playing on this tour only has been something I've really enjoyed and I feel like the guys have enjoyed having me come over and playing," said Reed.

"I don't feel any different. I feel like the guys have accepted me from day one.

"I can see how some of the guys would sit there and have an issue with guys coming over and just playing the big events.

"I've come over and played everything from big events, small events, events in the middle. I feel like it hasn't been any different for me."

Meanwhile, six-time major winner Rory McIlroy said that LIV was in "such a state of flux" and that the DP World Tour had been "more than accommodating" to the players seeking to leave the competition.

"The DP World Tour are well within their rights to change the rules and regulations," said McIlroy in his press conference prior to the Thursday start of the DP World India Championship.

"This is a way to protect their business and to make the tour as strong as possible."

On Tuesday he told Bloomberg he would vote to have LIV Golf defectors back on the PGA Tour and believed the breakaway circuit was no longer a threat to traditional tours.

articles.title: Reform faces criticism after councillors filmed making racist comments
articles.summary: Reform says all of those people filmed by ITV are under investigation having resigned or been suspended.
articles.body:
Warning: This report contains racist and offensive language.

Reform UK has said "there is no room for racism" in its party after ITV News broadcast undercover filming, gathered over a year, of some of its councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language.

In the film, Undercover: A Year in Reform, a Reform councillor and deputy mayor of Solihull is recorded calling Asian homeowners "parasites".

Labour described the investigation as "truly sickening" adding: "Nigel Farage can't shrug these latest revelations off as being a few bad apples."

A Reform spokesman said: "Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced" and that in some cases there had been suspensions.

The spokesman added that the party had improved its procedures but some individuals who did not share their values would occasionally make it through vetting.

ITV's filming involved eight figures in Reform – the BBC does not know how many it spoke to in total.

Reform says the people filmed by ITV are all under investigation, and have already either resigned or been suspended.

ITV News says it had reporters undercover with Reform UK candidates and councillors across England and Wales running up to the elections in May and four by-election campaigns this year and last.

These reporters joined a Reform councillor, Alan Feeney, in Solihull, in the West Midlands, where he was campaigning to retain his seat on the council, having defected from the Conservative Party in 2025.

He told undercover reporters the area has been "infested" with Asian families, and called them "absolute parasites".

Later in the film, he is recorded saying: "I'd be saying no more than one per cent of British population can be non-white."

The BBC has tried to contact Feeney for a response. ITV has reported that on Monday evening he had "mutually agreed" to resign from Reform UK, citing "personal reasons," and would be continuing as an independent councillor.

Reform Party leader Nigel Farage has repeatedly said he wants to get rid of those he has called "bad apples."

Two years ago he said he didn't want Reform to be "a sectarian or racially based party in any way at all".

"I'm going to be absolutely ruthless about it," he said.

In a statement released after ITV's film was broadcast, Reform said the party "had improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting".

The Conservatives said: "Nigel Farage promised to make Reform ready for government. These sorry individuals are proof he has failed."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "This is chilling. I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community."

A Green Party spokesman said: "Vilifying migrants and Muslims is Reform's main focus, and these racist comments reflect party policy."

articles.title: Vikings legend still thinks about missing out on the rushing record
articles.summary: Former Vikings RB Adrian Peterson still thinks he could have broken the single-season rushing record with another opportunity in 2012.
articles.body:
Former Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson produced one of the greatest rushing seasons in NFL history in 2012. After returning from a torn ACL suffered on Christmas Eve in 2011, Peterson came back stronger than ever, running for 2,097 yards.

His best moment came in Week 17 against the Green Bay Packers. The Vikings needed to win to make the playoffs, and everyone expected Peterson, who entered the game 208 yards short of Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record, to be the focal point of the offense again.

Even though the Packers knew Peterson was getting the ball, he still ran for 199 yards and scored two touchdowns (one receiving). Tied at 34 with 26 seconds left in regulation, Peterson took a handoff and burst through the line of scrimmage, evading Green Bay defenders en route to a 26-yard run that set Minnesota up at the Packers' 12-yard line.

Head coach Leslie Frazier let the clock run down to three seconds before calling a timeout. Then kicker Blair Walsh came in to boot the 29-yard field goal through to send the Vikings to the playoffs.

14 years later, Peterson still wishes he had another opportunity before that field goal to break the record.

"Hindsight when I think about, I'm like, 'God, dog, Coach Frazier, man, there [were] like 20 seconds left before I made that last run,'" Peterson told Jordan Schultz in an interview this week. "We could've called a timeout and given me another... run or two to get [the record]."

This was a criticism from fans at the time, though it never really made sense. Had Minnesota elected to call timeout and tried another run with Peterson, there was no guarantee he wouldn't have fumbled it, as that had been an issue throughout his career.

There could also have been any number of penalties, like a false start or holding that would have pushed Walsh back further. Worse yet, there could have been a risk of injury in a moment where the Vikings were in good position for a game-winning field goal.

Peterson came close to the record, and it would have been awesome to see him break it. But even if he wishes the end of the game had played out a little differently, the reality of the situation made it virtually impossible to accommodate the star running back.

articles.title: Will Zalatoris to undergo another major back surgery, will miss 2027 PGA Tour season: 'I've been through four years of hell'
articles.summary: Will Zalatoris is preparing for his third major back surgeries in the past four years.
articles.body:
Will Zalatoris will miss even more time due to his lingering back injury.

Zalatoris revealed on Wednesday at the media day for the PGA Tour's Austin Championship that he will undergo a spinal-fusion surgery late next month. That means that Zalatoris will miss the entire 2027 campaign.

It marks the third major back surgery Zalatoris has undergone since 2023.

"I've been through four years of hell, so it's good to have something that will hopefully correct it," Zalatoris said, via Golf.com . "It's not something you want to do, but when you have three Tour physical therapists tell you it needs to be done at some time, you go ahead and do it."

Zalatoris missed several months during the 2022 campaign due to two herniated discs in his back. Then, just before the Masters the following spring , he withdrew and underwent surgery on his back. That ended the 2023 campaign.

The injury has essentially lingered ever since. He said that he hurt his back again playing in San Antonio at the Valero Texas Open.

He recovered after his most recent back surgery last year and appeared in four events this season, but missed the cut in two of them and then finished T67 at the Valero Texas Open in April. He's not played competitively since.

Zalatoris was once a very promising golfer on Tour. He picked up his inaugural win at the 2022 FedEx St. Jude Championship, and he finished second at the Masters in 2021. Zalatoris had a stretch in which he finished top 10 in six of seven major championships, including a playoff loss at the PGA Championship in 2022 and a T2 run at the U.S. Open a month later.

But Zalatoris has missed the cut in his last four major championship outings, and has only played in 15 tournaments over the past two seasons. He's plummeted to No. 610 in the Official World Golf Rankings, too.

While Zalatoris will play in Austin, that'll be it until 2028. Hopefully by then, he said, he'll be in a much better spot.

"It's all connected together, and I just want to get it fixed," he said. "I can't promise anybody anything because of what I've been through. I'm the oldest 30-year-old you will ever meet."

articles.title: Rory McIlroy Chases Race To Dubai Title Against Patrick Reed
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy hunts a record-equaling Race to Dubai title in New Delhi, facing his longtime rival Patrick Reed in a showdown with no middle ground.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy has a specific goal in mind this week in New Delhi. He wants to capture his eighth Race to Dubai title. That would tie the all-time record held by Colin Montgomerie. But the path to that trophy is blocked by a familiar face. Patrick Reed currently leads the standings, while McIlroy has won the race for four consecutive years.

The two men are meeting on a new battleground in India, a place Reed had visited before this event existed. They share a decade of history, from the 2016 Ryder Cup to the 2018 Masters. Now they are back chasing the same points.

The dynamic between these two has shifted dramatically since the golf world fractured. After Reed departed the LIV Golf league and received a PGA Tour suspension, an opportunity arose for him to compete on the DP World Tour. He has won on the circuit since his return. McIlroy, meanwhile, supported the creation of the DP World India Championship to hunt new experiences.

Yahoo Sports reports that on Tuesday at the Delhi Golf Club, the pair exchanged a smile and a short conversation during a photo opportunity. They have been complimentary all season. Reed noted at the BMW PGA Championship that he relishes the chance to compete against McIlroy. "Any time I get to go play against Rory, it's always fun because that means you get to play some amazing golf," Reed said.

McIlroy stated that he requires no additional motivation to commit fully. "Yeah, look, I'm motivated regardless of who it is," he said at Wentworth.

While the players compete for points, the broader war over the sport's future appears to be ending. McIlroy is confident the threat from the rebel league is gone for good. In New Delhi, while speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, he addressed the probability of a second LIV Golf iteration launching.

McIlroy stated at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that launching version 2.0 of LIV seems difficult, noting that with each passing day, another former LIV player declares they will not return to LIV 2.0. He believes the league mismanaged its massive financial resources. "LIV had probably like half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy said. He argued the capital could have been used to partner with governing bodies instead of enriching pros who were already wealthy.

The landscape has changed with players like Jon Rahm, David Puig, and Adrian Meronk reportedly leaving the Saudi-backed league. Even Sergio Garcia had his contract terminated. McIlroy recalled his early stance against the breakaway. "Tiger and I, at the very start back in 2022 when this thing kicked off, we were certainly the two that were maybe the most vocal against it," McIlroy said.

Now, the choice for any player considering a return to the breakaway is stark. "You see Guy Kinnings coming out this week and saying that if LIV does go ahead in this 2.0 version, players that are thinking of going that direction, they're gonna have to make a choice," McIlroy said. "It's either you play LIV 2.0, and you can't play the DP World Tour, or you play the DP World Tour, and you can't play LIV 2.0. But I think this period of trying to double dip and do both is over."

This week's event in India represents more than just a tournament. It is the culmination of a decade-long rivalry and a test of the unified game. Reed is looking to become only the second American to win the Race to Dubai, joining Collin Morikawa. McIlroy is just one title shy of the record he covets. The fact that they are both there, competing on the same course, signals a new era.

The tension that once existed between the two tours is gone. The focus is now on performance and the points that matter most. Reed holds the lead, but McIlroy has the momentum and the experience of winning this race multiple times. The handshake in New Delhi was a sign of respect, but the competition on the course will be fierce. Both men are chasing a legacy-defining trophy.

The DP World Tour schedule continues with high stakes for both golfers. The Race to Dubai concludes at the end of the season, making every shot in India critical. McIlroy's comments suggest he sees the future of golf as stable and unified. The departure of major players from LIV and the bankruptcy filing in September have accelerated that shift.

If the league tries to reboot, it will face a wall of players who want to return to the traditional order. For now, the attention remains on the green in New Delhi. The battle for the title is on, and the history between these two rivals will play out in real time.

articles.title: Público pode escolher nome de macaco que nasceu no Parque Chico Mendes | G1
articles.standfirst: Filhote nasceu em 9 de julho, mês em que foi comemorado 30 anos do Parque Ambiental Chico Mendes. Votação é on-line e público poderá escolher entre os nomes Nino, Caju e Xingu.
articles.summary: Filhote nasceu em 9 de julho, mês em que foi comemorado 30 anos do Parque Ambiental Chico Mendes. Votação é on-line e público poderá escolher entre os nomes Nino, Caju e Xingu.
articles.body:
Filhote macho de macaco-barrigudo nasceu em 9 de julho no Parque Ambiental Chico Mendes, em Rio Branco — Foto: Val Fernandes/Secom

🐒🌳 Um novo morador do Parque Ambiental Chico Mendes, em Rio Branco , ainda não tem nome definido, mas isso está nas mãos do público.

É que um filhote macho de macaco-barrigudo, que nasceu em 9 de julho deste ano, poderá ser chamado de Nino, Caju ou Xingu , e a população pode participar da escolha por meio de uma votação on-line até o final de outubro.

👉 O nome Nino é uma opção curta e fácil de lembrar. Já Caju faz referência à natureza e à identidade brasileira, enquanto Xingu remete à identidade amazônica.

Além disso, a escolha do nome é uma forma de aproximar a população do trabalho de conservação desenvolvido no parque.

As opções foram selecionadas pela prefeitura de Rio Branco e buscam destacar características como a ligação com a natureza e a identidade amazônica.

Segundo a instituiçao, a iniciativa marca mais um momento especial para o parque, que completou 30 anos de inauguração em 31 de julho e registrou, com o nascimento do filhote, a primeira reprodução dessa espécie no local.

A revitalização do parque contou com investimento de cerca de R$ 1,5 milhão. Entre as melhorias, estão a pintura dos recintos do zoológico, dos banheiros e de áreas de convivência, além da recuperação da trilha asfaltada, da reconstrução da passarela de acesso ao zoológico e da renovação dos jardins. O parque também recebeu placas solares e passou a oferecer internet gratuita aos visitantes.

Com 57 hectares de floresta preservada, o local reúne trilhas ecológicas, zoológico com animais da região amazônica, áreas de recreação e academia ao ar livre.

Parque Chico Mendes passou por uma revitalização — Foto: Marcos Araújo/Secom

O espaço também abriga o Memorial Chico Mendes, dedicado à história do seringalista e ativista ambiental acreano assassinado em 1988.

Em 2024, o parque recebeu o selo internacional de sustentabilidade Good Travel Seal , concedido pela Fundação Green Destinations, da Holanda. Na época, foi divulgado que o espaço era o primeiro da Região Norte a receber a certificação, que avalia critérios como gestão de resíduos, energia, prevenção da poluição e acessibilidade.

O macaco-barrigudo (Lagothrix lagothricha) é um primata nativo da Amazônia. A espécie tem pelagem densa e costuma apresentar uma cauda longa e preênsil, que auxilia na locomoção pelas árvores.

Esses animais têm papel importante na manutenção das florestas, principalmente por contribuírem para a dispersão de sementes.

Ao se alimentarem de frutos e circularem pela mata, ajudam a espalhar sementes por diferentes áreas, favorecendo a regeneração da vegetação.

articles.title: 'It was suicide, not murder': Model Shraddha Dubey breaks silence in Shiva Sharma death case
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A day after being named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, model and social media influencer
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A day after being named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey surfaced in a video posted on social media, denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials and said she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.The 1-minute-15-second video emerged even as Lucknow Police intensified efforts to trace the accused. On Tuesday, police announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.In the video, Dubey alleged that rumours were being spread about her and objected to what she described as attempts to link her to politicians and bureaucrats based on social media associations.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she said, appealing to the media not to draw conclusions without evidence.Dubey also denied that she was absconding and claimed she intended to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said.Dubey asserted that Sharma’s death was not a murder. “The truth is that Shiva Sharma did not die due to murder but by suicide,” she said, adding that she was currently not in a condition to explain the circumstances in detail because of her health.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following the incident, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim that investigators are examining.All those named in the FIR remain untraceable. articles.title: PGA Tour Champions players livid after losing pension fund amid league's growth: 'It's actually criminal'
articles.summary: The senior tour has been offering golfers some sort of pension plan since the mid-1980s.
articles.body:
Billy Andrade is livid after learning that the PGA Tour Champions, the PGA Tour's senior circuit, has eliminated the pension program for golfers this week.

The PGA Tour used to offer the senior tour a $10 million pension program before it was cut to $8 million last year. Now, the Tour is opting to do away with the program altogether.

"You've got all these millions flowing everywhere for Championship Series, this series, that series, for all these leagues this guy [new PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp] is creating, and then they're taking this money that has been designated to these Champions players," Andrade said, via Golfweek . "These are the players who helped make the Tour what it is today and helped create the jobs that executives and current players enjoy ... It's actually criminal."

The news was delivered at the PGA Tour Champions' first player meeting of the season by president Miller Brady. The goal that was relayed to the players, per the report, was that the PGA Tour Champions wants to stand on its own financially in the future.

Previously, the pension program had been approved yearly. It started with a $250,000 allocation in 1985, and was a near-constant ever since. The only real break was when it was suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic. Players could qualify by playing in at least 12 tournaments each season, and they earned retirement credits by finishing in the top 48 in an event.

Brady said the senior circuit, which is available for golfers age 50 or older, is at a place where they are making real money on their own. The financial performance of the tour, he said, "is as good as it's ever been."

"While you never want to take anything away from the players, they also understand. They get it," Brady said. "I told the guys, it's my job to raise prize money over time, and we've slowly started to do that. For a long time, we were just happy to renew sponsors."

Though the PGA Tour Champions has undoubtedly grown in recent years — several regular-season tournaments have committed to having $3 million purses next season to match the five major championships, for example, and new tournaments are coming in — players clearly aren't happy to be losing money.

"They're playing for $20 million almost every week [on the PGA Tour], and they can't afford $10 million for our pension? It's a bad look, in my opinion, and I think most of the guys out there feel that way," David Toms said.

Stewart Cink is the current leader on the Charles Schwab Cup money list with nearly $3.8 million earned in 2026. Zach Johnson isn't far behind at $3.3 million earned.

Andrade earned roughly $12.5 million during his PGA Tour career, where he won four times, and he's won more than $9.1 million on the senior circuit. Toms, with 13 PGA Tour wins, earned nearly $42 million in his career. He's won five times on the PGA Tour Champions and earned nearly $10.3 million.

While nobody wants to lose money, players competing week-in and week-out on the senior tour have a great retirement gig. It's a 54-hole format where players are allowed to ride in carts, and a few million dollars are up for grabs at each tournament.

As far as retirement plans go, this one is hard to beat. And with the PGA Tour Champions growing the way it is, there's going to be only more money available for players in the future.

"The PGA Tour is a business. The powers that be are trying to run it like a business," Paul Goydos said. "The books are what they are. You can't run deficit spending. "Is it disappointing? Yes, it's not good. But it's understandable."

articles.title: Rory McIlroy’s encore, Tommy Fleetwood’s own opera: Golf’s big stage awaits
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Race To Dubai leader Patrick Reed saw a monkey running across the fairway at No. 13.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Race To Dubai leader Patrick Reed saw a monkey running across the fairway at No. 13. “Never seen that,” he said, grinning after the Wednesday Pro-Am outing at the India Championship.The teeming wildlife at Delhi Golf Club was there to keep him company, because for all the kids and their parents, all roads lead to the 18th, where Rory McIlroy’s bobbing figure emerged. The six-time Major winner broke into childlike laughter, clearly enjoying the day as he glowed in the afternoon sun.The round done, everyone was scrambling to get a piece of the World No. 2. Left profile, right, front, selfies clicked, and caps signed until he was whisked away in a buggy.The serious stuff begins on Thursday. There is a tournament to be won, and the race is on as the golfers see the $4 million WIC as an approach shot to the business end of the ‘Back 9’ series.The goalposts change. Rory, whose childhood dream was to “win all four Majors and be the best in the world” has ticked his boxes. Now, the focus is on equalling Colin Montgomerie’s record of claiming eight European Order of Merit titles.“Eugenio (Chacarra) jumped over me to second place last week in Spain. With Patrick missing the cut last week, I think this is really a good opportunity this week to cut into that lead and head to the Middle East in a really good spot.”Eye on the prize for now, but there’s plenty ahead for the 37-yearold who seemed to have conquered all his demons, having won the Masters twice in a row “Obviously the Majors will always be important. I want to make the Ryder Cup team.”“A lot of plates spinning,” the global golfer admitted. “There’s international golf, but obviously the bulk of my play is in America.”With his stature, comes a lot of responsibility too. He points to others. “If it’s a golfer’s prep, practice, diligence, work ethic, everything that he does off the course, it would be Aaron Rai,” he spoke glowingly of the PGA Championship winner.And then there’s Tommy Fleetwood, the defending champion, with whom he will be teeing off in the morning. “I always love watching Tommy hit balls in practice.”Sweet, mild-mannered Tommy had conducted his own rock opera in his hometown of Southport during this year’s Open Championship. “I was achieving a dream that I had as a seven-year-old boy at that very golf course. It was like having your own concert,” said the man from the Liverpool suburbs, who had finished tied-4th.It did not reach that crescendo, but he will always be grateful. “Not everybody gets those moments and those experiences.”Last year, he celebrated on the closing greens of DGC with his son Frankie, another emotional high. articles.title: Huge data centre and solar farm plans near King's Lynn revealed
articles.summary: The developers, Evolution Power Limited, say the two sites could attract £25bn of investment.
articles.body:
Plans have been drawn up for a huge new data centre and one of the UK's largest solar farms near King's Lynn in Norfolk.

Developers behind the Longmarsh Green Energy project said the data centre would require up to 1 gigawatt (GW) of power at any given time, while the solar farm the firm wants to build would generate up to 1.3GW.

Evolution Power Limited (EPL) said it was seeking to construct two sites covering around 4,695 acres (1,900 hectares) and the proposals could attract £25bn of investment.

A spokesperson said the project was "critical for future UK economic growth" and it had begun a consultation on the plans.

While details released about the project have been limited, the solar farm could generate more power than any other currently planned for the UK.

Developers behind the controversial High Grove scheme - one of the largest proposals which is also planned for rural Norfolk – say it would generate up to 720 megawatts (MW) of electricity, enough for 363,000 homes.

That is just over half what the newly proposed site is said to be capable of producing.

The solar farm would also include battery storage.

Meanwhile the accompanying data centre would require up to 1GW of electricity at any one time.

Boy knife attacker will not give evidence in trial

Pig abuser sentenced after being caught on camera

'Misguided' plan for travellers site rejected

EPL said one site for the project would be south of the A47 near the village of Tilney St Lawrence, with the other close to the villages of Fincham and Barton Bendish.

Along with drawing on solar energy, they would be connected to the existing electricity substation at Walpole, with the company aiming to have them operational by 2032.

It said the work would create thousands of construction jobs, while there would be more than 500 "direct operational roles" on site.

It added that it would use a "closed loop cooling system" – where liquid is recirculated – rather than taking water from the mains.

Such centres, which are used to store, process and transmit information, are frequently being opposed by local communities across the country, often due to environmental concerns.

But the government has deemed them critical to "nearly all economic activity and public services".

EPL said it expected to formally submit its planning application next April.

Because of its scale, it will be deemed a nationally significant infrastructure project (NSIP), which means final say will rest with the government rather than the local council.

Other major schemes, such as High Grove, have also been classed as NSIPs.

Referring to that and projects including a large wind farm also planned for the area, North West Norfolk Conservative MP James Wild said the new plan "could represent further large scale industrialisation of the landscape".

Alistair Beales, the independent leader of King's Lynn and West Norfolk Borough Council, said the authority would "do our job locally and reflect residents' concerns".

A spokesperson for EPL said its plans would "bring significant local and national economic benefits, providing secure renewable energy and data centre capacity".

They also said they would welcome feedback in a community consultation, which is running until 26 November.

articles.title: Chacarra comienza coliderando el India Championship el día que McIlroy cambia de 'look'
articles.standfirst: La primera jornada no se pudo completar por una tormenta eléctrica
articles.summary: La primera jornada no se pudo completar por una tormenta eléctrica
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra sigue tocado por la varita mágica de los dioses del golf. Tras su segundo puesto el pasado domingo en el Open de España, el madrileño ha empezando coliderando, junto al norirlandés Tom McKibbin, el DP World India Championship tras una primera jornada que no pudo completarse por una tormenta eléctrica. Chacarra acabó el día con 55 golpes (-5) tras jugar los 15 primeros hoyos del recorrido, fruto de seis birdies y un solo bogey. El español abrió su exhibición con sendos putts, de seis y cinco metros, en los hoyos 10 y 11 y cometió su único error en el 16 tras una mala salida. Un fallo que compensó de inmediato con un nuevo birdie en el 17 fruto de otro fabuloso putt de 8 metros. Los truenos y relámpagos que azotaban el Delhi Golf Club propiciaron que se suspendiera el resto de la jornada -con varios jugadores sin comenzar siquiera su recorrido-, en la que destacó también Nacho Elvira (-2 tras 13 hoyos) en la duodécima posición. Chacarra persigue una histórica victoria en la Race to Dubai, que premia cada año al mejor golfista del DP World Tour. Un trofeo que ya ganó Jon Rahm en 2019. Sus dos principales rivales son el estadounidense Patrick Reed -que hoy no salió de tee- y el norirlandés Rory McIlroy, que busca su quinto entorchado consecutivo y el octavo de su prodigiosa carrera. Precisamente McIlroy fue el gran protagonista de esta primera jornada pero más por su 'look' que por su juego, pues lució unos pantalones holgados al más puro estilo Tommy Fleetwood. Entre los espectadores que siguieron su recorrido de cerca, por dentro de las cuerdas, se encontraba el mismísimo Ronaldo Nazario. El ganador de seis Majors jugó 14 hoyos para acabar empatado con el reseñado Elvira, a tres golpes de los colíderes. "En mi día a día, cuando no tengo que usar mi uniforme de golf, suelo usar pantalones de pierna ancha. Es lo que está de moda, lo que marca tendencia.", había explicado McIlroy en la previa del torneo.

articles.title: Cuando los problemas de espalda frenan una de las carreras más brillantes del golf
articles.standfirst: Will Zalatoris habla de su "infierno" y anuncia que no jugará en 2027 porque se someterá a una operación de fusión espinal
articles.summary: Will Zalatoris anuncia que no jugará en 2027 porque se someterá a una operación de
articles.body: Will Zalatoris tiene hoy 30 años y ocupa el puesto número 610 del ranking mundial. Los problemas de espalda están truncando la carrera de un golfista que en su día irrumpió con fuerza en el mundo profesional y que rápidamente se convirtió en un gran jugador de Majors, aunque no llegara a levantar ninguno. En el Masters de 2021 no estuvo lejos de convertirse en el primer novato que ganaba el torneo desde 1979, pero finalizó en segunda posición. El estadounidense ha demostrado siempre ser un jugador formidable, llamado a ser de los mejores del mundo, pero su nombre cada vez suena menos debido sus problemas de espalda. Ahora ha anunciado que se someterá a otra operación que, según él, le obligará a perderse toda la temporada 2027 del PGA Tour. En 2022 estuvo cerca de hacerse con el PGA Championship, edición recordada por el colapso de Mito Pereira, pero perdió en el playoff contra Justin Thomas. Después ganaría su primer y único torneo en el PGA y se colocaría séptimo del ranking mundial; una semana después se retiraría del BMW Championship por problemas de espalda y desde entonces ya no ha vuelto a competir con regularidad. Aquel mágico 2022 estuvo en la pelea por tres de los cuatro grandes. Este año dejó de jugar en abril y ahora vuelve a para disputar el Austin Championship, pero con las mismas ha anunciado que se someterá una operación de fusión espinal a finales de noviembre. “He pasado por cuatro años de infierno, así que es bueno tener algo que, con suerte, lo alivie”, comentó Zalatoris antes la prensa. El californiano, agregó resignado: “No es algo que uno quiera hacer, pero cuando tres fisioterapeutas del Tour te dicen que hay que hacerlo en algún momento, simplemente lo haces”. Esta será la tercera intervención importante de espalda a la que se somete Zalatoris, tras una microdiscectomía en 2023 y un reemplazo de disco artificial en 2025. Participó en cuatro torneos este año antes de perderse el resto de la temporada por una rotura del labrum de la cadera derecha. “Todo está relacionado y solo quiero solucionarlo. No puedo prometerle nada a nadie por lo que he pasado. Soy la persona de 30 años más mayor que jamás conocerás”, añadió el golfista. No es ni será el primer golfista con problemas serios de espalda. Hay muchos casos y en España por ejemplo Seve Ballesteros o José María Olazábal tuvieron bastantes problemas en este sentido; Fred Couples, Tiger Woods, Jason Day o Rory McIlroy saben lo que es lidiar con este tipo de lesiones.

articles.title: Labour to break from Green council groups that back Zionism policy
articles.summary: Labour says it will end power-sharing deals with councillors that do not disown the party's new stance.
articles.body:
Labour has said it will end power-sharing agreements with the Green Party on local councils, unless its councillors disown the party's newly-adopted policy that Zionism is a form of racism.

Labour says it will give local Green groups seven days to confirm they reject the policy, which was recently approved by Green members at its party conference.

The ultimatum applies to 18 councils where it shares power with the Greens, either directly or alongside other parties.

The Greens hit back at the move, accusing Labour of meddling and arguing it would be undemocratic for the party to "tell local parties what to do".

The policy motion adopted by members of the Green Party of England and Wales said Zionism was an ideology that supported an "ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians.

It backed the creation of a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

It has led to a backlash from Jewish groups, as well as criticism from senior Green figures, including four of its five MPs.

Green leader Zack Polanski, who skipped the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, has said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.

He has however said that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by racist ideology", arguing this was the "substantial part" of the motion. Israel has denied committing genocide in Gaza.

The party's two deputy leaders have been at odds over the policy, with Mothin Ali backing the move and Rachel Millward voting against it.

Labour is currently in coalition with the Green Party on local councils in Sheffield, Lewes and Warwick. In other areas, it runs the council as part of a broader coalition alongside other parties.

Burnham rules out coalition with Greens after 'Zionism is racism' motion

Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs Labour would not partner with the Greens over the "antisemitic" policy, although Downing Street did not confirm what this meant for local government.

The party has now said it wants all local Labour groups to write to their Green counterparts, demanding "clear and unambiguous" statements rejecting the policy.

Green groups will also be asked to call on their party's "national leadership" to reconsider the policy.

"Where they are unable to provide that assurance, Labour will bring any such local arrangement to an end," the party's chair Bridget Phillipson said.

In response to Burnham's comments, Polanski said: "I'm the only Jewish leader of a political party. I'm a victim of antisemitism every day and I've made it clear Jewish people are welcome in my party."

A Green Party spokesperson said: "For the Labour government to conflate criticism of Israel with antisemitism is disappointing and wrong.

"Trying to tell local parties what to do and who they can work with is undemocratic."

The Board of Deputies of British Jews, the UK's largest cross-community Jewish organisation, welcomed Labour's announcement.

Its vice president Karen Newman said the Greens had adopted an "antisemitic platform", adding of Labour's position: "This is a commitment we have been pressing for, and we are urging other mainstream parties to take the same clear and principled stand."

National parties exercise various levels of control over groups of local councillors who wish to do deals to govern locally.

Labour councillors require the approval of its ruling National Executive Committee before entering into local tie-ups.

According to the party's rulebook, local groups must also "stand down" from power sharing arrangements when asked to do so by their regional office.

By contrast, the Green Party of England and Wales allows local groups to make the final decision on where and whether to share power locally.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Tom McKibbin one shot off lead in India, Rory McIlroy three further back
articles.summary: Tom McKibbin is one shot off the lead and Rory McIlroy three further back after a weather-disrupted opening day of the DP World India Championship.
articles.body:
DP World India Championship, day one leaderboard

6 N Norgaard (Den); -5 T McKibbin (NI), E Chacarra (Spa), T Detry (Bel); -4 S Jamieson (Sco), R MacIntyre (Sco), E Ferguson (Sco), O Prakash Chouhan (Ind), M Armitage (Eng), A Meronk (Pol) (5*); -3 B Robinson Thompson (Eng), H Townsend (Swe)

Selected others: -2 R McIlroy (NI), T Fleetwood (Eng); Level J Rose (Eng), L Donald (Eng); +3 S Lowry (Ire)

* Denotes number of holes played before play ended on day one

Tom McKibbin sat one shot off the lead, with fellow Northern Ireland player Rory McIlroy a further three shots back, after a severely weather-disrupted opening day of the DP World India Championship in New Delhi.

Denmark's Niklas Norgaard topped the leaderboard on day one after a six-under-par round of 66 which included an eagle, six birdies and two bogeys at the Delhi Golf Club.

McKibbin, Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra and Belgian Thomas Detry all reached five under as they completed their opening rounds.

Play was suspended because of lightning and torrential rain shortly after 06:30 BST, and did not resume until five hours later, leaving many of the field unable to finish their first 18 holes and preventing others from starting their rounds.

McKibbin posted six birdies, with his card marred by a solitary bogey, to put himself well in contention.

Starting at the 10th hole, the 23-year-old picked up shots at four consecutive holes from the 12th to the 15th, before dropping a shot at the par-four 16th.

Further birdies at the 18th and the third elevated him to joint top spot, before Norgaard moved a shot ahead with a scintillating late charge of one eagle and five birdies in his final seven holes.

McKibbin's sole DP World Tour win to date came in the European Open in Germany in 2023 and since January 2025 he has been part of the LIV Golf tour.

He has secured top-six finishes at the British Masters and Irish Open on the DP World Tour this season.

A trio of Scots - Scott Jamieson, Robert MacIntyre and Ewen Ferguson - sit three under, along with India's Om Prakash Chouhan and Marcus Armitage of England.

World number two McIlroy bogeyed the first hole of his round, the 10th, but reacted with birdies at the 13th, 15th, 18th and second holes, before giving up a further shot to par on the third.

The back-to-back Masters champion finished on the same two-under mark as Englishman Tommy Fleetwood.

McIlroy sat third in the Race to Dubai standings before this week's tournament, behind leader Patrick Reed and second-placed Chacarra.

articles.title: Jon Rahm Gives Up Remainder of $300M LIV Golf Contract as Part of Separation Agreement
articles.summary: It appears that Jon Rahm was willing to do anything to get out of his LIV Golf contract, even if it meant leaving a massive amount of money on the table.
articles.body:
It appears that Jon Rahm was willing to do anything to get out of his LIV Golf contract, even if it meant leaving a massive amount of money on the table.

Per ESPN's Mark Schlabach , as part of Rahm's separation agreement with LIV Golf for the return of his exclusive name, image and likeness rights, the 31-year-old gave up the remainder of his $300 million contract. Schlabach noted that "it is believed that Rahm was owed more than $100 million over the remainder of his contract," which he signed in December 2023 after leaving the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf.

Trump's golfer granddaughter undergoes wrist surgery

According to Schlabach, court records showed that Rahm was LIV Golf's largest unsecured creditor, and he "was owed $7.5 million when the league voluntarily filed for Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8." A month later, it appears that he was owed much more.

During his three-year LIV Golf tenure from 2024 to 2026, Rahm made nearly $107 million in on-course earnings. He was the season-long individual champion in all three years in the breakaway league.

Despite his success while competing in LIV Golf, Rahm's attorney, John Beck, informed U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey Judge Michael B. Kaplan on Oct. 7 that his client won't be joining LIV Golf 2.0.

"Mr. Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0," Beck said at the time.

Kaplan is expected to approve Rahm's separation agreement from LIV Golf on Nov. 5. The two-time major champion is scheduled to play in the Abu Dhabi Championship on Nov. 5-8, the second-to-last event of the DP World Tour season. Schlabach noted that it is "unclear how quickly Rahm will be allowed to return to the PGA Tour if that's what he desires."

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Rory McIlroy four off clubhouse lead after thunder and lightning delays in first round
articles.summary: Weather caused four-hour suspension to play on Thursday in New Delhi; Rory McIlroy and Tommy Fleetwood finish on two under, four behind clubhouse leader Niklas Norgaard; first round continues on Friday; watch tournament until Sunday on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
McIlroy was midway through the back nine when play was stopped for thunder and lightning in the area, with players then off the course for over four hours.

When play did resume at 4pm local time, McIlroy completed a round of 70 to sit tied 13th.

The world No 2 started from the par-four 10th, which he bogeyed, and went out in 34 after birdies at the 13th, 15th and 18th.

He found another birdie at the second hole but followed that with a second bogey of the round at the third, before finishing with six successive pars.

Denmark's Niklas Norgaard holds the clubhouse lead on six-under thanks to a 66, with McIlroy's fellow Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin one of three players at five-under with Eugenio Chacarra, who is second in the Race to Dubai standings.

"Yeah, it was okay," McIlroy, who sits third in the Race to Dubai rankings, said of his first round.

"I felt like I hit the ball pretty well for the most part. Missed a few putts early on, got it going a little bit around the middle and then maybe missed a couple opportunities when we came back out after the delay.

"So overall, it felt like it could have been a couple better but still a solid start. No one's really getting away.

"The golf course is playing a little bit tougher than it did last year just with how long the rough is. So we'll see how much we play tomorrow, we're not sure. But yeah, it's a solid start and obviously still a lot of golf left to play."

Scottish trio Scott Jamieson, Ewen Ferguson and Bob MacIntyre all shot opening rounds of 68.

Tommy Fleetwood dropped two shots at his final hole, the ninth, to finish on two-under alongside McIlroy after finding the bushes with his tee shot and having to play out sideways.

Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed was among the later groups to start after the weather delay and so only completed four holes, although was two-over already.

The final four groups did not tee off at all with the first round to resume on Friday.

articles.title: Rahm renuncia a una millonada para desvincularse de LIV Golf
articles.standfirst: El golfista español llega a un acuerdo con LIV para separar sus caminos
articles.summary: El golfista español llega a un acuerdo con LIV para separar sus caminos
articles.body: Jon Rahm ya ha alcanzado un acuerdo con LIV Golf para desvincularse formalmente de la liga. Ayer se presentó una moción en el proceso de quiebra de LIV para aprobar una ‘separación y liberación mutua con Jon Rahm’. El ‘León de Barrika’ quedará libre contractualmente de dicho circuito una vez se obtenga la aprobación del juez, programada para una firma en una audiencia el 5 de noviembre. Ambas partes acordaron una 'separación' de mutuo acuerdo, aunque para ello tuvieron que realizarse concesiones. Rahm retira su reclamación de 7.5 millones de dólares y renuncia a cualquier otra reclamación que haya ocurrido antes de que el acuerdo entre en vigor. Por su parte, LIV no podrá demandar al golfista por algo derivado de su contrato con ellos. Los citados 7,5 millones se corresponden con la cantidad que cobra por contrato, concernientes sólo al trimestre previo a que LIV decretara la suspensión de pagos. Cabe recordar que el golfistas vasco aún tenía varios años más de vínculo con el LIV, por lo que realmente está renunciando a una suma millonaria. En cualquier caso, esto no tiene nada que ver con la cantidad ingresada en premios durante los tres años de estancia en esta competición, que es de unos 100 millones de dólares que sí habrían sido satisfechos. El vizcaíno, que ha permanecido tres años en la liga, recupera sus derechos de imagen, con salvedades como que LIV aún puede usar contenido histórico suyo. El nombre del equipo 'Legion XIII' y la marca relacionada se entregan a la compañía de Rahm, pero este no podrá usarlo en competiciones de golf por equipos, es decir, si recalara por ejemplo en TGL (liga indoor creada por McIlroy y Tiger) o si el PGA creara franquicias. Por otro lado, Jon tendrá también el control total sobre la marca 'Rahmbo'. El acuerdo es una desvinculación económica total entre Rahm y LIV Golf, como así dicen los documentos entregados al juez. El golfista no hará reclamaciones “por honorarios, bonificaciones, indemnizaciones, daños por rescisión, premios en metálico, pagos anuales, comisiones por compromiso y otras reclamaciones de pago—, con el fin de lograr una desvinculación económica total”.

articles.title: Jon Rahm officially walks away from LIV Golf and the estimated $100M still owed to him in deal
articles.summary: Jon Rahm agreed to forfeit the remainder of an estimated $100 million still owed to him as part of his official separation deal with LIV Golf.
articles.body: Jon Rahm is officially out of LIV Golf, and it's costing him. The two-time major winner reached a separation agreement with the league in which he agreed to forfeit the remainder of the estimated $100 million owed to him. Rahm will have his name, image, and likeness rights returned to him as part of the deal, ESPN reported, citing court records. Rahm shocked the golf world nearly three years ago when, after publicly dismissing the league, he joined it on a deal that was rumored to be between $300 million and $600 million. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But at a bankruptcy hearing last week, Rahm's attorneys stated that he would not be part of what has been dubbed "LIV 2.0" and its "unacceptable" terms. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey last month. Between 2021 and 2026, LIV spent an estimated $5 billion to $8 billion. Bankruptcy filings show the league owes millions of dollars in unpaid compensation to top players, including Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cam Smith. The PIF halted funding in April to redirect money toward domestic projects and manage financial pressures from the regional war with Iran. Following the decision, PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan resigned from LIV’s board. Rahm won the league's individual title in each of the last three years, making his defection from the league arguably its biggest hit. The rest of the golfers have until Oct. 25 to decide whether they will stay for LIV 2.0 or follow in Rahm's footsteps. There is a chance the league will cease operations. LIV golfers were allowed to play on the DP World Tour as long as they were in good standing and paid any fines for playing in LIV events that conflicted with the DP World Tour calendar — those fines were paid for by the PIF until 2025. Rahm won the 2021 U.S. Open and the 2023 Masters. He and Tyrrell Hatton were the lone LIV golfers on Team Europe during last year's Ryder Cup. LIV has laid off most of its operational staff, left event contractors waiting for payment and faces a lawsuit from the Premier Golf League alleging breach of confidence and conspiracy. Brooks Koepka was the first big name to leave LIV Golf, doing so late last year and returning to the PGA Tour. Patrick Reed followed in his footsteps shortly after. articles.title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion
articles.summary: The party was reported to the Equality and Human Rights Commission by MPs and antisemitism campaigners.
articles.body:
The equality watchdog has written to the Green Party asking for more information about a controversial "Zionism is racism" motion passed by members.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) said it recognised that "many Jewish people will be feeling vulnerable" following the motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month.

The motion described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".

In a response to the ECHR letter, the party said it "will not discriminate against or exclude people for holding Zionist views" and was committed to tackling antisemitism.

Dozens of Labour and Lib Dem MPs and Jewish campaigners wrote to the regulator raising concerns about antisemitism after the Green motion was passed.

Alongside Jewish groups, the motion was criticised by four of the five Green MPs and two former leaders, one of whom said it was "dangerous" and "divisive".

It piled some pressure on Green leader Zack Polanski in the wake of a by-election defeat. He said the motion was "imperfect" and he wanted to see it amended.

Labour has said it will end power-sharing agreements with the Greens on local councils, unless its councillors disown the motion.

On Thursday, the EHRC confirmed it had written to the Greens following the complaints received.

A spokesperson for the watchdog said: "We have written to the Green Party of England and Wales about its recently adopted 'Zionism is racism' motion to ask for more information and assess its practical implications and potential impact.

"We have received complaints alleging unlawful activity under the Equality Act 2010, including concerns that Jewish people could face discrimination because of their beliefs following the adoption of the motion."

The watchdog said it would "take action where appropriate" after assessing the extra information.

"In the case of the Green Party motion, compliance with the Equality Act is likely to hinge on the practical effects of the motion," the spokesperson added.

In a letter earlier this month , some MPs raised concerns not only about the motion itself but also amendments to protect Jewish Green members at Zionist synagogues being voted down.

"Taken together, these developments raise serious questions about whether Jewish members can participate freely and equally in the party, and whether their religious and communal connections could expose them to complaints or disciplinary action," their letter said.

Separately, the Campaign Against Antisemitism wrote to the EHRC alleging the party had breached the Equality Act through discrimination against Jews.

The campaign group said the motion "effectively states that the state of Israel should not exist" and "defines support for a Jewish homeland in any form as racist".

Having been backed by members, the motion has become party policy but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

In response to the EHRC letter, the Green Party of England and Wales said it "will not discriminate against or exclude people for holding Zionist views" and the motion sets out a political position with "no impact on membership conditions or internal disciplinary processes".

"The party's comprehensive antisemitism guidance, which forms part of our framework of ethics, remains unchanged," a spokesperson added.

"We remain committed to tackling antisemitism and ensuring Jewish members feel welcome and respected."

articles.title: UK Green member behind anti-Zionism motion ‘receives death threats’
articles.summary: Lubna Speitan, who has Palestinian roots, believes messages and emails are part of an effort to intimidate her.
articles.body:
London, United Kingdom – The British-Palestinian woman behind the Zionism is racism motion, passed by the Green Party of England and Wales earlier this month, says she has received death and rape threats since the vote.

In an interview with Al Jazeera on Thursday, Green member Lubna Speitan, an artist and activist, said she has received dozens of threatening social media messages and emails, which she has reported to the police.

“These threats were anticipated,” said Speitan, who believes they are a form of “intimidation” from pro-Israel agitators.

While “no one wants to be on the receiving end of death threats”, she said it is “necessary to confront these evils”.

The Greens passed the motion by 1,022 votes to 813 at their party conference in Brighton, but it has been criticised by virtually all other British political parties and has brought turmoil to the Greens.

Several of its left-wing MPs have criticised the move, and on Thursday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham ruled out partnering with the party, calling the motion “wrong” and “anti-Semitic”.

The motion defines Zionism, the belief that Jews have a historic claim to Palestine, as a form of racism, predicated on the dispossession and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians. Palestinians made up more than 90 percent of the population in 1917, when Britain declared its support for a Jewish state in the country.

The motion supports Palestinians’ right to self-determination and calls for the establishment of a single democratic state in historic Palestine for Muslims and Jews. It also says that anti-Zionism should not be equated with anti-Semitism.

Fifty-six members of Speitan’s family have been killed since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza three years ago.

“Zionism is defined clearly as an ethnonationalist settler-colonial project. The motion also recognises, correctly, that not all Jews are Zionists and not all Zionists are Jews,” she said. “It targets an ideology: Zionism.”

She added that she has been “personally smeared” by media outlets.

Recent headlines in the British press have claimed she was “friends” with an “al-Qaeda terrorist”, as she reportedly offered to testify in defence of Minh Quang Pham, a UK citizen who had planned an attack at Heathrow Airport.

“This tactic of guilt by association will not be dignified with a response,” Speitan said of the reports.

The Green Party of England and Wales told Al Jazeera that Speitan holds no party positions “other than being a member”.

“The Green Party takes all allegations of this nature seriously. Where members have expressed views that do not fit in with the party’s values, we have internal processes to investigate, and an investigation is under way,” it said.

Media watchdog NewsCord, which reviewed coverage of the motion, concluded that opponents of the resolution received 10 times more coverage than its supporters.

The Green Party is not the first Western political institution to classify Zionism as a form of racism . In 1975, the United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution declaring that Zionism was a racist ideology. Seventy-two countries voted in favour of the motion, while 35 opposed it and 32 abstained. The resolution was later repealed in 1991.

articles.title: LIV Golf bankruptcy process: DP World Tour accused of interfering after taking harder line on tour membership
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau and other LIV golfers have effectively been released from their contracts as part of the league applying for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; players could be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0, which is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital
articles.body:
The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support having ploughed in $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

But in order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of the existing players so they can be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0.

However, the DP World Tour confirmed this week it was taking a harder line than previously and any player committing to LIV 2.0 would be ineligible for its membership and therefore also ruled out of Ryder Cup contention.

It has been seen in many quarters as an attempt to deliver the final blow to LIV's fading hopes of survival and, according to reports in the US media, its attorney Robert Fitzgerald told the US Bankruptcy Court in New York: "We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly.

"The timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process, with our players and potentially our reorganisation writ large."

Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, said in a statement on Monday: "Players need to make a choice. As we have said for many years, we have rules and regulations which are there to protect our Tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our Tour."

Also at the US Bankruptcy Court hearing in New York, Judge Michael B Kaplan also approved a motion to reject the current contracts of 19 golfers after LIV stated they "do not reflect the contemplated compensation structure under LIV 2.0".

It means the likes of DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Bubba Watson and Lee Westwood are free to pursue other options should they wish.

Jon Rahm's release, confirmed at the hearing, has seen him give up all claims against LIV's bankruptcy estate, reported to be up to $150m (£113m).

LIV has given up nearly all rights to use Rahm's name, image, likeness, trademarks and branding going forward, while Rahm has retained control of his LIV team Legion XIII's intellectual property and trademarks.

The next hearing in LIV's bankruptcy case is scheduled for October 20, with a deadline for player commitments agreed between LIV and BC Partners set for October 25.

articles.title: Jon Rahm reaches agreement to end LIV tenure, walking away from as much as $100 Million
articles.summary: Rahm's departure is another blow to LIV Golf.
articles.body:
We've all been in relationships — business, professional, an awkward holiday party conversation — where we just wanted out . In the I've-had-enough moment, you'd be willing to give up a whole lot to extract yourself. But would you be willing to give up nine figures of owed revenue to get out of said relationship? Jon Rahm apparently was, and thus he's brought a decisive, definitive close to his days as a LIV Golf player and team captain.

Rahm and LIV have reached a separation agreement where the reigning LIV Golf individual champion and captain of Legion XIII will be free to leave the onetime breakaway tour. Equally significant: Rahm has released all claims on LIV for future money owed, a figure that could total as much as $100 million.

The separation agreement must be approved by a U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge on Nov. 5, per ESPN.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

LIV Golf is in an existential battle right now. The tour's Saudi-backed "Golf, but louder" days are nothing but a pastel and club-music memory. As it proceeds through bankruptcy, LIV is attempting to gather both investors and players for "LIV 2.0," a tour that would crisscross the planet while giving players the chance at unprecedented equity in the venture.

Rahm, however, decided to go a different path, and burned the boats behind him. "Mr. Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0," his attorney John Beck said earlier this month, "and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0."

As part of the separation agreement, Rahm will forgo all equity interest in the team which was formed upon his arrival in LIV three years ago. He will, however, retain the rights to his name, image and likeness, as well as terms such as "Rahmbo" and "Legion XIII," his team's name. (He won't be able to use "Legion XIII" in a golf context, such as a TGL team.)

Regardless of the potential value of team equity, Rahm was still owed a significant amount of money by LIV — more than $7 million as noted in bankruptcy documents, with a potential $100 million still remaining on his reported $300 million deal he originally signed with LIV. Rahm was LIV's largest unsecured creditor in bankruptcy proceedings.

It's impossible to view Rahm's stance as anything other than a severe blow to LIV's hopes for a second act. So much of LIV's appeal was based on the star power of its most notable players, with Rahm — the three-time individual champion — at the very top of that list alongside Bryson DeChambeau. With Rahm gone and DeChambeau still a free agent, LIV's attractiveness to investors drawn to golf celebrity has dimmed significantly.

For his part, Rahm is clearly demonstrating a willingness to put LIV Golf behind him. He'll likely need to play his way onto the PGA Tour the way his former LIV colleague Patrick Reed is doing; PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has not indicated he'll re-offer the rapid pathway that Rahm declined earlier this year. Rahm is next slated to play in the DP World Tour's Abu Dhabi Championship in the first week of November.

For LIV, these next two weeks will be crucial ones. The tour is attempting to determine whether it will even continue as a viable concern; LIV's attorney Robert Fitzgerald indicated this week that the tour will announce by the end of the month whether it's proceeding forward or closing down entirely.

Either way, LIV's days with Rahm are done. There were highlights, there were celebrations, there were substantial paychecks — but in the end, there wasn't enough to keep Rahm around any longer. And he was willing to give up an astounding amount to make the split permanent.

articles.title: Factory championing women workers named world’s best new building
articles.summary: A lush seven-story textile factory in Bangladesh has won the prestigious RIBA International Prize, with judges calling it a “work of quiet humility.”
articles.body: Featuring tranquil courtyards, pond-lined walkways and a facade bursting with tropical plants, a rug factory in Bangladesh has claimed one of architecture’s top prizes. Green Field Factory, a seven-story textile facility in the northern city of Rangpur, won the prestigious RIBA International Prize on Thursday, with judges calling the building a “work of quiet humility.” Set across more than 144,000 square feet, the factory was commended by the award’s organizer, the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA), for integrating greenery into its design. Landscaped gardens, verdant verandas and a main wall draped in plants helped “bring nature directly into the workplace,” the organization said in a press release. The Bangladeshi firm behind the project, Nakshabid Architects, was inspired by traditional Bengali homesteads, which are typically interspersed with courtyards and ponds. The biennial prize often honors community-focused projects, rather than eye-catching icons, and it was the architects’ focus on the approximately 5,000 — mostly female — employees that attracted particular praise from the jury. Amenities for workers include a rooftop daycare center, on-site medical practice and shady areas to socialize. A large statue of a female figure, which the architects said represents the “strength of women’s empowerment,” stands at the facility’s entrance. According to RIBA — whose judging panel visited the site in September — employees often use the factory’s amenities with their families outside working hours. The project presented an “alternative model for factory design and operation,” the organization added. Bangladesh is among the world’s largest textile producers, though conditions in the country’s factories are an ongoing concern among labor rights groups. In 2013, Rana Plaza, a nine-story building crammed with garment factories outside the capital Dhaka, collapsed killing 1,100 people. The disaster resulted from cultural as well as structural failures: factory workers’ safety concerns had been ignored, with many forced to return to the building after cracks were discovered. In stark contrast, Green Field Factory’s design prioritized employee wellbeing and challenged “ingrained social hierarchies,” RIBA said. In his citation, jury chair Bijoy Jain pointed to the huge central entranceway used by employees, managers and owners alike (in Bangladesh, it is common for laborers and senior staff to enter large factories via separate entrances), calling it an “equanimous shared portal.” In a statement published ahead of Thursday’s announcement, Nakshabid Architects’ founder and principal, Bayejid M. Khondoker, said he had wanted to “prove that industry can breathe, nurture and inspire.” “We asked a simple question: What if a factory were designed first as a home for the people who work in it?” he is quoted as saying. “Every courtyard, garden, water body and shaded verandah grew from that question. A factory should not be a machine that consumes human energy. It should be a living place that restores it.” Green Field Factory is operated by Karupannya Rangpur Limited, which, as well as handmade rugs, produces textile items like doormats and bathmats. It was one of two Bangladeshi projects on the prize’s four-building shortlist, alongside the climate-responsive BRAC University in Dhaka. The other two finalists, both in Belgium, were a thoughtfully renovated 1960s office building and a recently expanded art institute. Although only founded in 2016, the RIBA International Prize is arguably the most prestigious accolade awarded to a single building. Typically held every two years (although the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted this schedule), the prize honors projects that demonstrate “visionary, innovative thinking and design excellence.” The prize was last awarded in 2024, when it was won by a six-story timber social housing project in Barcelona, Spain. Other previous winners include a school in rural Brazil, a university in Lima, Peru, and a serene hospital in a remote, flood-prone area of Bangladesh.

The factory opened in 2017, though due to various circumstances such as the pandemic, RIBA's jury wasn't able to visit until this year.
Four of the seven-story factory's floors house areas for making textiles, with others containing packaging operations and a warehouse.
A large staircase leading to an entrance that, somewhat unusually for a large Bangladeshi factory, is used by all employees, regardless of seniority.
