articles.title: London suburban housing project wins top UK architecture award
articles.summary: Lion Green Road in Coulsdon was recognised for the way it responds to its surroundings.
articles.body:
A suburban housing development in south London has won the UK's most prestigious architecture award, with judges praising its sensitive design and integration into the surrounding landscape.

Lion Green Road in Coulsdon, comprising 157 homes across five distinctive 13-sided blocks, was named winner of the 2026 Stirling Prize by the Royal Institute of British Architects (Riba).

Designed by Mary Duggan Architects and built with RUFF Architects, it combines affordable and private housing for Croydon Council.

Replacing a former car park on a challenging, sloping site that varies in height by eight metres, Riba president Chris Williamson praised the design as a "new approach to higher density development" creating "a new connection between the bustling Lion Green Road and a distinctive area of green parkland beyond".

Duggan said the win was "extraordinary, unexpected and humbling".

"Lion Green Road began in 2016 with a very clear vision, to create genuinely non-institutional housing and to think differently about what affordable housing could offer commnities.

"We think of Lion Green Road as a project about the culture of dwelling... architectural ambition, social value and social realities can co-exist."

Williamson told the BBC that until he went to study architecture he lived in a council estate in the East Midlands, "and every time I go back there all the council houses have been sold off, they're in private hands.

"Which in a way can be a good thing - we're in a homeowning democracy - but the sad thing is they haven't been replaced.

"Every time I go back - without getting too emotional - I think 'where would we have lived?'

"So to me that's why this particular project was important. I think a lot of people from that sort of background live in terrible accommodaiton - temporary accommodation which isn't safe or secure.

"These houses are fantastic and they're part of a mixed scheme so it's got a fantastic feel to it.

"For me it was a very inspirational, emotional, part of the process."

Duggan, who was brought up in south-west London, said the scheme "challenged conventional suburban housing layouts centred on roads, private gardens and clearly defined front and back spaces".

Winding paths and planting weave between the blocks, connecting them and linking shared outdoor spaces.

She said she wanted it to be a public space people felt they could belong to.

"Housing needs to be progressive. People who live in the building have access to green space, allotments."

The site fronts onto Lion Green Road, with low-rise green belt housing set on higher ground to the south and traditional suburban streets to the north.

Nestled amongst trees on the edge of green-belt land, the development's soft purple and pink brickwork blends high-density housing into an area of natural beauty.

At a time when housing developments are often judged by their cost and number of homes they can deliver, the project was recognised for the way it responds to its surroundings.

Williamson said "the housing blocks blend into the parkland beyond, while small variations in pattern add texture and give each building its own identity."

He added: "The way it fits into the hillside - it doesn't look like a large housing scheme.

"It has community gardens, it's the sort of place i would have liked to have grown up in."

The project was funded by Croydon Council as a public asset, and a change in building regulations meant it "fought against five or six circumstantial elements beyond the normal challenges".

The building was praised by the jury for its "inventive and site-specific response to a highly constrained plot".

Buildings are assessed across a range of criteria, including design vision, innovation, sustainability, functionality, and the ability to delight users and visitors.

articles.title: Matthew Mayich’s Parents Slam ASU Coach’s Exit as ‘Negotiated Agreement’ Rather Than ‘Accountability’
articles.summary: The hockey player, who collapsed during a military-style workout, has a “zero chance” of recovering, his family’s attorney said
articles.body:
The family of Matthew Mayich is speaking out after Arizona State University announced it is parting ways with its hockey coach

In a statement, the family called the news "a negotiated agreement" instead of the university taking accountability for their son's medical emergency

Mayich collapsed, suffering heat stroke and losing oxygen to his brain, during an outdoor, military-style workout on Aug. 20

Matthew Mayich 's family is speaking out amid news that Arizona State University has parted ways with hockey coach Greg Powers, nearly two months after Mayich collapsed following a team workout.

"Our focus remains where it has been since August 20: Matthew, and making sure what happened to him is fully understood and never happens to another player," the family said in a statement on Thursday, Oct. 15. "It seems more like a negotiated agreement than accountability, and so we believe Justice Bales's investigation must continue with its full scope, covering everyone involved in that morning's workout and in approving it, and its findings must be made public."

The statement continued, "Coach Powers's departure should not limit his cooperation or anyone else's and the players who have spoken up must be protected. We wish Coach Hakstol, his staff and the players a safe and successful season."

Earlier on Thursday, ASU announced that it had mutually parted ways with coach Greg Powers.

The program announced Powers' exit in a statement and said Dave Hakstol, who was coaching for the Colorado Avalanche, would take over.

"We welcome Dave Hakstol and his family to Arizona State University," Sun Devil Athletics Director Graham Rossini said. "His success building championship-caliber programs, developing players for the highest level of the sport, and leading organizations in the NHL speaks to his knowledge of the game and his ability to develop talent."

Powers was put on leave on Sept. 30, more than a month after Mayich's medical emergency on Aug. 20, after the team worked out under the direction of a former Green Beret who had no affiliation with the school.

Mayich, 21, suffered heat stroke and lost oxygen to his brain after the military-style outdoor workout in 90 degree conditions and has "zero chance" of recovery , according to his family's lawyer.

The SEC student-athlete availability report was introduced in the 2024 season for conference games only.

The initial report is released on Wednesday of an SEC game week, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to kickoff of a Saturday game.

Prior to game day, players are designated by their school as available, probable, questionable, doubtful or out for the upcoming game. On game day, they are designated as available, game-time decision or out.

• Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play.

• Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play.

• Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play.

• Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play.

Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players' participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it.

Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses.

articles.title: QB Faizon Brandon remains questionable on SEC injury report for Tennessee vs Alabama
articles.summary: Tennessee football quarterback Faizon Brandon remains questionable for the Alabama game on the SEC student-athlete availability report on Oct. 15.
articles.body:
Tennessee football quarterback Faizon Brandon remains questionable for the Alabama game on the SEC student-athlete availability report on Oct. 15.

The report will be updated daily and then 90 minutes before the game.

No. 14 Tennessee (5-1, 2-1 SEC) plays No. 7 Alabama (5-1, 3-1) on Oct. 17 (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC) at Neyland Stadium.

A source told Knox News on Oct. 15 that MacIntyre would start against the Tide.

Brandon, a five-star freshman, started UT's first five games of the season, but he suffered a right shoulder injury in a 20-17 loss to Texas on Sept. 26. Brandon hasn't played since being benched in favor of George MacIntyre midway through a 24-14 win over Auburn on Oct. 3.

Coach Josh Heupel said Brandon was at the Arkansas game for "emergency use only" on Oct. 10. Brandon has been limited at practice this week, according to numerous reports.

Seven Tennessee players have already suffered season-ending injuries. They include starting left guard Wendell Moe , starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee), starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee), safety Dylan Lewis (foot), wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg), linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee) and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body).

Ryan Coleman-Williams out; Alabama starters on injury list

Some notable Alabama players appeared on the initial availability report, including three starters injured in a 20-17 loss to No. 1 Georgia on Oct. 10.

Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is out. He leads the team with 23 receptions, 415 yards and four TDs. Starting defensive lineman Terrance Green, who has 2.5 sacks, is also out. Starting center Racin Delgatty was downgraded from questionable to doubtful with a lower leg injury.

QB Faizon Brandon (questionable, right shoulder)

OL Wendell Moe (out for season, lower leg)

KR/WR Joakim Dodson (out for season, leg)

CB Jadais Richard (out for season, upper-body)

The SEC student-athlete availability report was introduced in the 2024 season for conference games only.

The initial report is released on Wednesday of an SEC game week, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to kickoff of a Saturday game.

Prior to game day, players are designated by their school as available, probable, questionable, doubtful or out for the upcoming game. On game day, they are designated as available, game-time decision or out.

• Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play.

• Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play.

• Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play.

• Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play.

Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players' participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it.

Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses.
